stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = x^{2} + bx + c\), where \(b\) and \(c\) are constants. The vertex of the graph of \(y = f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane is \((-3, -2)\). What is the value of \(f(1)\)?
solution: The leading coefficient is 1, so in vertex form \(f(x) = (x + 3)^{2} - 2\).
verify:
x, b, c = symbols('x b c')
f = x**2 + b*x + c
s = solve([Eq(-b/2, -3), Eq(f.subs(x, -3), -2)], [b, c])
assert s[b] == 6 and s[c] == 7
assert f.subs(s).subs(x, 1) == 14
assert Rational(spr_answers[0]) == 14
